scope: Thirty reproducible public-data studies with case-specific decisions, baselines, and external source records.

cases.title: Jersey City Bike Demand and Rebalancing Evidence
cases.gallery_title: Jersey City Bike Demand and Rebalancing Evidence
cases.question: Can station-hour history improve held-out pickup forecasts, and which fixed-budget rebalancing scenario deserves a bounded operations pilot?

source.dataset: Jersey City Bike Demand and Rebalancing Evidence
source.version: Jersey City trip history, January-December 2021; derived station-hour aggregate
source.grain: one station-hour-month aggregate

cases.result: Held-out station-hour MAE is 0.69 pickups/day, a 33.1% improvement over the hour-only baseline.
cases.boundary: Rebalancing outcomes are modeled; no stockout, routing, labor, or achieved-service claim.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Jersey City Bike Demand and Rebalancing Evidence

cases.title: Cross-City 311 Distribution Shift and Transfer Gate
cases.gallery_title: Cross-City 311 Distribution Shift and Transfer Gate

source.dataset: Cross-City 311 Distribution Shift and Transfer Gate
source.publisher: City of Chicago and City of New York
source.grain: one city-day-audited service-family aggregate

cases.result: The 2023 cross-city total-variation distance is 58.1%, and the transfer gate is refused.
cases.boundary: Administrative shift audit only; requests are not latent need or service quality.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Cross-City 311 Distribution Shift and Transfer Gate

cases.title: Capacity-Constrained Marketing Pilot
cases.gallery_title: Capacity-Constrained Marketing Pilot
cases.question: Can pre-contact information concentrate observed responses under a fixed outreach capacity without using post-contact leakage?

source.dataset: Bank Marketing
source.grain: one direct-marketing contact outcome

cases.result: The untouched test yields an AUC of 0.650 and a Brier score of 0.210; the top 5% captures 7.4% of observed responses.
cases.boundary: Observed response concentration is not incremental lift, causal treatment effect, profit, or return on outreach.

cases.gallery_title: ACS Employment AI Temporal Transport and Audit

cases.title: Treasury Curve and Tail-Risk Decision Engine
cases.gallery_title: Treasury Curve and Tail-Risk Decision Engine
cases.question: How do duration choices change historical tail loss, backtest behavior, and sensitivity to dependent market shocks?

source.dataset: Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates
source.grain: one U.S. Treasury business-day yield curve

methods: daily carry plus first-order duration response
cases.result: Historical ES95 loss rises from 0.4% for the short baseline to 0.9% for the long-duration portfolio; the short-baseline rolling VaR exceedance rate is 6.0%.
cases.boundary: First-order duration omits convexity, security selection, costs, financing, taxes, liquidity, and future-regime uncertainty.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Treasury Curve and Tail-Risk Decision Engine

cases.title: Human-in-the-Loop Complaint Triage Information System
cases.gallery_title: Human-in-the-Loop Complaint Triage Information System
cases.question: Does a privacy-minimized complaint model create reliable ranking gain over random review in a later calendar period?

source.dataset: Consumer Complaint Database: Money Transfer, Virtual Currency, or Money Service
source.version: Closed 2022 UTC date window; privacy-minimized extract created 2026-07-27
source.grain: one CFPB complaint received in 2022 for a money-transfer, virtual-currency, or money-service product

cases.result: The later-period AUC is 0.611 (block-bootstrap 95% interval 0.539 to 0.697), while top-5% lift is 1.00 (95% interval 0.33 to 2.46); the ranking model fails the deployment gate.
cases.boundary: The timely flag is not complaint merit, harm, resolution quality, company quality, or compliance; the 2022 model may not transport.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Human-in-the-Loop Complaint Triage Information System

cases.title: Commercial Real Estate Diligence Decision Product
cases.gallery_title: Commercial Real Estate Diligence Decision Product

source.license: NYC Open Data Terms of Use
source.grain: one public NYC property-sale record before robust analytical filtering

cases.result: Across 12,399 filtered commercial transactions, Manhattan has the highest borough median price per square foot at $743; the break-even cap rate at 8.5% debt is 7.5%.
cases.boundary: The source does not establish arm's-length status, NOI, expenses, occupancy, condition, appraisal value, debt terms, or causal regeneration effects.

cases.title: SEC N-PORT Liquidity and Crowding Filing Review
cases.gallery_title: SEC N-PORT Liquidity and Crowding Filing Review

cases.boundary: Filing review only; no expected-return, suitability, fund-quality, or investment recommendation.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for SEC N-PORT Liquidity and Crowding Filing Review

cases.title: Social-Norm Field Experiment with Household-Clustered Inference
cases.gallery_title: Social-Norm Field Experiment with Household-Clustered Inference

cases.title: Population Health Risk Transport Across NHIS Cohorts
cases.gallery_title: Population Health Risk Transport Across NHIS Cohorts

source.version: NHIS 2016 and 2017 Sample Adult files linked to 2019 public-use mortality
source.grain: one NHIS sampled adult linked to mortality status

cases.result: The 2017 temporal test yields an AUC of 0.846 and weighted two-year mortality of 2.32% across 58,754 linked adults.
cases.boundary: Population-risk validation only; no individual diagnosis, treatment, or clinical deployment.

cases.gallery_title: Opportunity Zone One-Year Policy Evidence Screen

source.grain: one Massachusetts tract-year row

cases.boundary: Associational one-year screen; no causal effect because parallel trends are unavailable.

cases.title: Small-Sample Repeated-Measures Inference
cases.gallery_title: Small-Sample Repeated-Measures Inference
cases.question: How does passage type change eye-movement burden within the same participant, and how stable is the contrast across reader groups?

source.dataset: Eye movements of dyslexic and average readers in meaningful and pseudoword passage reading
source.grain: one de-identified study participant with repeated passage measures

cases.result: Across 57 complete participant pairs, the mean pseudoword-minus-meaningful fixation-duration difference is 34.25 (bootstrap 95% interval 25.87 to 43.35), with a Holm-adjusted sign-flip p-value of 0.0003.
cases.boundary: The public sample is small and does not establish downstream educational outcomes or an intervention effect.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Small-Sample Repeated-Measures Inference

cases.title: NHANES Mortality Transportability and Population Inequality
cases.gallery_title: NHANES Mortality Transportability and Population Inequality

source.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics
source.version: NHANES 2011-2012 and 2015-2016 demographics linked to 2019 mortality
source.grain: one NHANES adult linked to 36-month mortality

cases.result: The external-cohort check yields an AUC of 0.804 and a Brier score of 0.022 across 11,820 linked adults.
cases.boundary: Population research only; no individual diagnosis or treatment.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for NHANES Mortality Transportability and Population Inequality

cases.title: Spatial Equity Planning with Transit and Site-Evidence Gates
cases.gallery_title: Spatial Equity Planning with Transit and Site-Evidence Gates
cases.question: Which tract-level service-hub priorities merit local review after observed rapid-transit proximity is added?

source.dataset: Spatial Equity Planning with Transit and Site-Evidence Gates
source.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau and Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority
source.version: 2019-2023 ACS tract estimates, 2023 Gazetteer, and MBTA rapid-transit stops accessed 2026-08-10
source.license: U.S. Government open data and MBTA open data
source.grain: one Massachusetts census tract

headline_metrics.label: Site decision
headline_metrics.value: blocked pending land and feasibility evidence

cases.result: Across 1,597 analyzed tracts and 265 rapid-transit stop records, the high-poverty weighted nearest-stop distance is 40.65 km.
cases.boundary: No site recommendation until parcel, zoning, network, cost, and community evidence is supplied.

cases.title: When a Blood Pressure Survey Changes Its Measurement Protocol
cases.gallery_title: When a Blood Pressure Survey Changes Its Measurement Protocol
cases.question: How much does replacing a blood-pressure measurement protocol change a survey threshold count?

source.dataset: NHANES 2017–2018 blood pressure methodology study and demographics
source.grain: One examined adult with at least two valid systolic readings in each protocol

cases.result: Across 4,614 paired adults, the survey-weighted automatic-minus-manual mean was -1.50 mmHg. At 130 mmHg, 5.32% moved above and 8.15% moved below the cutoff.
cases.boundary: The device and examiner change together. Weighted results describe adults with paired examination records; threshold crossings are survey classifications, not new clinical diagnoses.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for When a Blood Pressure Survey Changes Its Measurement Protocol

cases.title: When Should a Wrist Monitor Withhold a Heart Rate Reading?
cases.gallery_title: When Should a Wrist Monitor Withhold a Heart Rate Reading?
cases.question: When can a wrist monitor's quality gate reduce error without leaving users without readings for too long?

source.dataset: PPG-DaLiA daily activities and WESAD laboratory sessions
source.publisher: Attila Reiss et al. / UCI and Philip Schmidt et al. / Universität Siegen
source.grain: One non-overlapping eight-second activity window from an anonymized participant

cases.result: With the DaLiA threshold frozen, WESAD retained 85.2% of 5,544 eligible windows. Subject-averaged absolute error among reported ECG-readable windows was 6.83 bpm.
cases.boundary: The ECG reference is algorithm-derived. The external cohort changes the activity setting; both studies use Empatica wrist hardware. Reported accuracy applies only to the activity and ECG eligibility definitions.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for When Should a Wrist Monitor Withhold a Heart Rate Reading?

cases.title: When Should a Call Centre Reallocate Staff After a Demand Shock?
cases.gallery_title: When Should a Call Centre Reallocate Staff After a Demand Shock?
cases.question: When, within a fixed staffing budget, should a manager release temporary service capacity?

source.dataset: Technion Service Engineering Israeli bank call-centre logs
source.license: Public academic research data; publisher terms apply
source.grain: One queued telephone call between 08:00 and 13:00 on a Sunday–Thursday business day

cases.result: Across 65 held-out mornings, mean simulated abandonment was 17.23% with a fixed reserve and 18.48% under receding-horizon dispatch. Observed abandonment averaged 13.91%.
cases.boundary: Historical outcomes describe observed calls. Staffing schedules, patience past the censoring point, operator flexibility and policy-dependent waits are simulated. The five-hour morning replay begins with an empty queue.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for When Should a Call Centre Reallocate Staff After a Demand Shock?

cases.title: Which State Unemployment Claims Alerts Survive the Next Release?
cases.gallery_title: Which State Unemployment Claims Alerts Survive the Next Release?
cases.question: Which state-level claims alerts survive the switch from first publication to claimant-residence reporting?

source.dataset: Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims, advance state tables
source.grain: One US state or covered territory and initial-claims week, with two actual release dates

cases.result: Across 68 held-out weekly releases at 5 review slots, 83.2% of first-release alerts and 89.7% of revision-adjusted alerts appeared in the next release's residence-based list.
cases.boundary: The advance column is reported by liable state and includes a workshare proxy. The next release uses state of residence. The ranked target is a later published measure, not a directly observed employment shock.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Which State Unemployment Claims Alerts Survive the Next Release?

cases.title: Maintaining Earliest Arrival Routes Across Timetable Revisions
cases.gallery_title: Maintaining Earliest Arrival Routes Across Timetable Revisions
cases.question: Can a router repair a revised timetable and still return exactly the same earliest arrivals as rebuilding?

source.dataset: MBTA archived GTFS timetables for common service date 22 November 2024
source.grain: One changed scheduled connection or version marker in ordered MBTA archive copies

cases.result: Across 10 timetable versions, all 300 route-query results matched a full scan. Revisions changed 4,223 destination arrival labels; checkpoint repair visited 1,969,278 connections versus 8,903,454 for full recomputation.
cases.boundary: The archive assigns each download a non-overlapping archive interval. This is a comparison of overlapping planned calendar service inside those files. Results concern scheduled travel in a selected network, with a stated same-station transfer buffer and no street-walking links.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Maintaining Earliest Arrival Routes Across Timetable Revisions

cases.title: The Last Review Slot in an Online Queue
cases.gallery_title: The Last Review Slot in an Online Queue
cases.question: When should an online reviewer spend the last daily slot on the current edit?

source.dataset: Wikimedia MediaWiki history, English Wikivoyage
source.license: Wikimedia historical dumps; attribution and terms of use
source.grain: One timestamped main-namespace English Wikivoyage revision, with complete future label horizon

cases.result: Across 366 held-out publication days, the inventory-value policy captured 308 seven-day identity reverts, versus 287 with a fixed threshold and 1095 for an outcome-aware upper bound.
cases.boundary: An identity revert indicates that previously observed page content returned within seven days. It is a behavioral proxy. The replay assumes no effect of the simulated review on subsequent edits.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for The Last Review Slot in an Online Queue

cases.title: Where Should a Marketplace Spend Its Delivery Improvement Budget?
cases.gallery_title: Where Should a Marketplace Spend Its Delivery Improvement Budget?
cases.question: Should a marketplace direct an equal number of review slots to seller handoffs or to post-handoff delivery?

source.dataset: Olist Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset
source.grain: One order with exactly one recorded item from one seller; incomplete outcomes are retained

cases.result: Across 4 future quarters and 2,000 equal review slots per policy, adjusted seller targeting found 86 late deliveries following a missed handoff deadline. Carrier-focused targeting found 225 late deliveries after on-time handoff.
cases.boundary: An on-time handoff followed by a late delivery locates delay in the observed sequence. It does not establish fault or show that an intervention prevented lateness.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Where Should a Marketplace Spend Its Delivery Improvement Budget?

cases.title: Knowing When to Fall Back After a Drive Fleet Changes
cases.gallery_title: Knowing When to Fall Back After a Drive Fleet Changes
cases.question: When monitoring signals disappear after a fleet change, is switching to an interpretable rule worth the lost warnings?

source.dataset: Backblaze Hard Drive Daily Statistics, 2016
source.license: Backblaze Drive Stats terms and attribution
source.grain: One maximal consecutive run of equal binned SMART indicators for a pseudonymous drive

cases.result: With 15 daily review slots across 139 held-out dates, event recall was 21.8% for the pending-sector rule and 9.8% for monitored fallback across 459 observable failures.
cases.boundary: A recorded hardware failure is a proxy for replacement need. A late and an absent failure are distinguishable only while the drive remains observed. Alternative dispatch rules are replayed on logged outcomes.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Knowing When to Fall Back After a Drive Fleet Changes

cases.title: How Much Departure Delay Can a Last-Mile Route Absorb?
cases.gallery_title: How Much Departure Delay Can a Last-Mile Route Absorb?
cases.question: How late can a dispatcher release a route while still honoring its published windows and a stated end of shift?

source.dataset: Amazon Last Mile Routing Research Challenge, public model-build inputs
source.publisher: Amazon / MIT Last Mile Routing Research Challenge
source.grain: One stop in a complete route, including its row of the fixed travel-time matrix

cases.result: On 24 complete published routes, window-focused relocation produced 10 nonnegative departure-delay witnesses; the recorded sequences produced 10. 14 routes remained inconclusive under the search budget.
cases.boundary: Package time windows and driver sequences are observed. Travel times are a provided static matrix, service durations are planned, and the depot-return deadline is an eight-hour scenario. Unsolved routes remain undetermined.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for How Much Departure Delay Can a Last-Mile Route Absorb?

cases.title: How Much Inspection Capacity Should a City Reserve for Random Audits?
cases.gallery_title: How Much Inspection Capacity Should a City Reserve for Random Audits?
cases.question: How much of a city's finite inspection capacity should be reserved for random exploration?

source.dataset: Chicago Food Inspection Forecasting, historical permits and canvass inspections
source.license: City of Chicago open data and repository license
source.grain: One active retail-food license with a previously identified restaurant at the start of a quarter

cases.result: The 25% exploration policy allocated 960 slots over 8 quarters. Historical results were observable for 197 selections, giving full-roster critical-finding bounds of 4.9% to 84.4%.
cases.boundary: In the archival data only inspected restaurants reveal violations. The roster requires a known prior restaurant classification; never-classified premises are outside the target. Later inspections do not identify the causal effect of scheduling earlier.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for How Much Inspection Capacity Should a City Reserve for Random Audits?

cases.title: Counterexamples or Direct Corrections for Novice Programmers?
cases.gallery_title: Counterexamples or Direct Corrections for Novice Programmers?
cases.question: Should a beginner receive an elicited counterexample or a direct correction after a repeatable misconception?

source.dataset: CSEDM 2019 published ITAP cross-validation rows and the Refactory novice programming corpus
source.publisher: Thomas Price and CSEDM 2019 organizers and Yang Hu and coauthors
source.version: Public challenge demonstration and predictions, revision 6e7a1f6463d6343bd0c063fdeacf9cf9147e5073 / ASE 2019 public artifact, f05583a56c2e3c50aa8cc0327645283f27df3a68
source.license: Publicly released example; full DataShop records have separate terms
source.grain: Either an author-published learner/problem summary or an independently published anonymized source-code attempt

cases.result: The authors' public file contained 729 learner–problem records. On 584 matched out-of-time learner-held-out observations, first-correct F1 was 0.676 for the past-only model. In the independent code archive, 27 incorrect programs removed from the list being traversed.
cases.boundary: The public CSEDM example describes a subset of the 89-learner, 38-task source cohort. It contains aggregated learner/problem outcomes. Actual code examples are from the independent Refactory study. No newly delivered hint or transfer improvement is attributed to either cohort.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Counterexamples or Direct Corrections for Novice Programmers?

cases.title: Cut Credit Exposure or Hedge Rates During a Corporate Bond Drawdown?
cases.gallery_title: Cut Credit Exposure or Hedge Rates During a Corporate Bond Drawdown?
cases.question: During a credit drawdown, how does reducing corporate exposure compare with matching its expected rate sensitivity using a Treasury hedge?

source.dataset: Issuer historical NAV and ex-dividend distribution records for LQD, IEF, SHY and TLT
source.publisher: BlackRock iShares and the Federal Reserve
source.version: Aligned calendar years 2004–2025 / Board GZ spread and H.15 10-year yield
source.license: Copyright BlackRock; issuer terms of use
source.grain: One common trading week for four iShares funds

cases.result: Over 1097 held-out weeks, the rule triggered 143 times. The modeled net maximum drawdown was -17.02% after cutting credit and -19.21% under the matched-rate hedge.
cases.boundary: A backtest using fund NAVs is a modeled portfolio. Shorting and funding spreads beyond the stated transaction cost can change the comparison. The non-rate residual includes liquidity and issuer-specific risk.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Cut Credit Exposure or Hedge Rates During a Corporate Bond Drawdown?

cases.title: How Reliable Are Model Comparisons With Overlapping Evaluation Windows?
cases.gallery_title: How Reliable Are Model Comparisons With Overlapping Evaluation Windows?
cases.question: How wide should a forecast-comparison interval be when adjacent scores reuse six days of observations?

source.dataset: EIA-930 hourly balancing authority electricity load
source.grain: One balancing authority and UTC date with 24 observed, forecast and lagged observations

cases.result: Across 1,520 shared dates after the source-quality screen and 6 balancing authorities, the day-ahead minus seasonal-naive score averaged -5.14 percentage points. The 95% HAC interval spanned 0.943 points versus 0.304 under independence.
cases.boundary: The public extract contains historical reported observations, including revisions. Known-truth coverage is a simulation estimate with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Estimates concern the six reported balancing areas.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for How Reliable Are Model Comparisons With Overlapping Evaluation Windows?

cases.title: When Reported Earnings Outrun Cash Collections
cases.gallery_title: When Reported Earnings Outrun Cash Collections
cases.question: When earnings outrun collections, do receivables and inventory changes improve next-year cash-flow forecasts?

source.dataset: US SEC EDGAR as-filed US-GAAP facts with an Apple audited-note cross-check
source.publisher: US SEC EDGAR; fixed public mirror by DenyTranDFW and Apple Inc.
source.version: Point-in-time accession facts, mirror revision e4088db1b10363c29719508935991a851587d17c / 2023 Form 10-K, accession 0000320193-23-000106
source.license: Public filings; mirror metadata and terms linked
source.grain: One issuer, accession and fiscal period in an original or comparative annual filing

cases.result: Across 89 out-of-time company-year forecasts, next-year operating-cash-flow MAE was 3.08% of opening assets for cash persistence and 3.07% for the accrual model.
cases.boundary: Predictive associations in a selected panel do not establish manipulation or causality. Vendor non-trade receivables are distinct from customer trade balances. Scenario valuations depend on payout, opening book, abnormal-return persistence and cost of equity.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for When Reported Earnings Outrun Cash Collections

cases.title: Consistent Road Geometry During Interrupted Map Updates
cases.gallery_title: Consistent Road Geometry During Interrupted Map Updates
cases.question: Can an interrupted map update publish mutually consistent node positions and road geometry?

source.dataset: Geofabrik OpenStreetMap Monaco extracts and regional daily replication diffs
source.grain: One base/oracle OSM element or one ordered node/way edit or sequence marker

cases.result: Across 29 consecutive real map releases, dependency-aware repair matched every full rebuild and the next independent snapshot (3,655 highway geometries). Updating only revised ways missed 1 geometry-version discrepancy.
cases.boundary: This is a reproducible experiment on a single regional OSM extract and a local SQLite store. Work counts measure recomputation. System latency and production availability require separate measurement.
cases.figure_alt: Representative evidence figure for Consistent Road Geometry During Interrupted Map Updates
